meta.title: SLATE research: access for a wheelchair user, and when the people a person knows are free
meta.method: Web research on 2026-10-02. confirmed:true means the figure was read on the publisher's own page or document (operator, regulator, statistics office, government). confirmed:false means it came from a search summary, a press report, Wikipedia or a third-party guide, usually because the publisher's page refused the fetch (TfL, HUD web pages, CDMX government servers, citizensinformation.ie, vancouver.ca and newhavenct.gov all returned 403 or refused the connection). A figure marked derived was computed here by arithmetic from published figures; the inputs are given in the note. null means no figure was found; nothing was estimated.
meta.fetchCaveat: Some confirmed:true figures were read through a page-summarising fetch rather than raw text. Where a raw copy was obtainable (curl or PDF text), it was checked directly: StatCan LFS tables, CSO LFS Q2 2026, INEGI ENOE bulletins, NTA SPSV Bulletin 2025, LADOT taxicab rules, the HUD AHS reports, the EHS 2018-19 fact sheet, the TfL taxi action plan, the Toronto 2024 vehicle-for-hire report, CTtransit and the Connecticut OLR report. BLS pages refused curl; their figures were read through the fetch twice, with a request for verbatim sentences.

transit.note: AccessibleNYC 2025 report (Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities). The 493 includes Staten Island Railway stations. The MTA's own station list (https://www.mta.info/accessibility/stations, updated 2026-09-14) lists the accessible stations but prints no count. The share is derived: 155/493.
'All New York City Transit buses are fully wheelchair accessible by front-door ramp (local and Select Bus routes) or lift (for coach-style buses on express routes).'

transit.mode: Metro-North Railroad (New York State service area)
transit.note: Covers Metro-North's seven New York counties only. It does not cover the New Haven Line stations in Connecticut.

transit.unit: share of rail stations and buses wheelchair accessible
transit.note: 'All Metro buses and rail lines are wheelchair accessible.' and 'Every rail station has a ramp, walkway or elevator to the platform.' If an elevator is out of service, the rider may take a bus to the next station at no extra cost.

transit.unit: share of buses with a wheelchair lift or ramp
transit.note: 'All buses have wheelchair lifts or ramps for people with disabilities to access. Also, the bus can "kneel" to lower the first step height.'
Not found. The 70-of-85 figure covers New York State stations only.

Wikipedia, 'as of January 2026'. The TTC's own page (https://www.ttc.ca/accessibility/Easier-access-on-the-TTC/Elevators-and-Escalators) lists the elevators but prints no count. It says Easier Access Phase 3 makes all remaining stations accessible except Old Mill by 2027. A TTC project page says Greenwood became accessible in February 2026, so the count may now be 64.

transit.unit: share of bus routes run with low-floor accessible buses
transit.note: Wikipedia says all bus routes have been run with low-floor accessible vehicles since 2015. Not read on ttc.ca.
'All of our stations are equipped with elevators for people using wheelchairs or other mobility devices.'

The page gives no fleet share. It says some stops are not set up for safe boarding with a mobility aid, and that some four-wheel scooters have a turning radius too wide for the conventional bus fleet.

TfL press release of 26 March 2026: 94 step-free Tube stations after Colindale (December 2025); 'more than a third of the Tube network'. The 272 total came from search results, not from this release, and Northolt was due to go step-free in summer 2026. The share is derived: 94/272. tfl.gov.uk returned 403.

transit.mode: Elizabeth line, DLR, trams and London Overground
transit.unit: share of Elizabeth line, DLR and tram stations step-free
transit.note: '...over half of London Overground stations and all Elizabeth line stations, DLR stations and tram stops have step-free access.' A London Assembly answer seen only in search results says all 41 Elizabeth line stations are step-free from street to platform.
'TfL's fleet of around 9,000 buses are all wheelchair-accessible, and around 94 per cent of TfL's 19,000 bus stops are also accessible.'

transit.unit: share of stops and trams wheelchair accessible
transit.note: A third-party guide says Luas was 'designed to be fully accessible'. The Citizens Information page refused the fetch, and the TFI accessibility overview gives no figure.

TFI (publisher) recommends 4 hours' notice for staff assistance and says DART, Maynooth and Northern Commuter lines have 31 stations in 13 zones, each zone with a staffed hub. A third-party guide says nearly all DART stations are step-free except Greystones, Killiney and Sutton (unconfirmed). No count was found.

transit.unit: share of routes run with low-floor wheelchair-accessible buses
transit.note: Third-party guide. Not read on the operator's site.

transit.unit: stations actually accessible to people with disabilities
transit.note: Milenio, 31 December 2024. The official network map marks 85 of 195 stations as universally accessible, but Milenio's investigation found only 57 working. metro.cdmx.gob.mx refused the connection. The share is derived: 57/195. The 85/195 share would be 0.436.

Search summary of a Metrobús press note: 202 of 207 stations on six lines accessible, 98%. The publisher's server refused the connection. The date of the note is unclear and Metrobús now has seven lines.
Not found. Search results say new RTP electric buses have ramps and kneeling, but give no fleet share.

paratransit.note: Rule confirmed on the publisher's page: 'Access-A-Ride fare is the same as the full fare on fixed-route bus and subway.' Exact change on boarding; a personal care attendant rides free. The $3.00 amount is the base fare from 4 January 2026, and it was seen only in a search summary of https://www.mta.info/document/190086.

paratransit.figure: 1-2 days ahead, 7 a.m.-5 p.m., 7 days a week; no same-day trips
paratransit.note: 'Reservations can be made 1-2 days in advance, 7 days a week, from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m.' and 'Same-day trips are not available.'

paratransit.unit: USD per one-way trip under 20 miles
paratransit.note: $2.75 up to 19.9 miles; $3.50 for 20 miles or more; $2.00 in Santa Clarita and Antelope Valley.

paratransit.figure: day before, by 10 p.m. (lines open 6 a.m.-10 p.m.); no same-day
paratransit.note: 'You must schedule your ride a day in advance.' Santa Clarita and Antelope Valley close at 8 p.m. The page gives no maximum days ahead.

paratransit.service: Greater New Haven Transit District ADA paratransit
paratransit.note: Exact fare, and drivers cannot make change. Book 1 to 7 days ahead, by 5:00 p.m. the day before; no same-day requests or changes. Covers origins and destinations within 3/4 mile of a fixed route.

paratransit.unit: CAD per trip (regular TTC adult fare, PRESTO or card)
paratransit.note: Wheel-Trans runs 'under the regular TTC fare structure'. The amount is from https://www.ttc.ca/Fares-and-passes: $3.30 by PRESTO or card, $3.35 cash. Booking (https://www.ttc.ca/wheel-trans/booking-your-trip-and-the-day-of-your-trip): advance trips from the next day up to 7 days ahead; same-day trips at least 4 hours before pickup or drop-off.

From 1 July 2026. Adult monthly pass $117.20; concession cash $2.30 and pass $66.95. 'You can book your trip as far as seven days in advance and until 4 p.m. the day before your trip.' A search summary instead gave $3.35 cash and $2.70 stored value; the publisher's page figure is used. Online booking is expected in 2027.

TfL's own blog, November 2023: 'a free, door-to-door transport service for older and disabled Londoners'. Advance bookings: one per day, up to 7 days ahead, at most one return journey a week. Next-day and same-day journeys have no limit but depend on availability. Search results give hours of 07:00-22:00, seven days a week. tfl.gov.uk returned 403.

No public door-to-door paratransit equivalent was found. Dublin relies on accessible scheduled services, staff assistance booked ahead (Irish Rail recommends 4 hours' notice), Dublin Bus's free Travel Assistance Scheme (third-party source) and wheelchair-accessible taxis.
No government paratransit service was found. Only private wheelchair-taxi firms appeared in searches.

taxis.unit: share of active yellow taxis wheelchair accessible (more than)
taxis.note: 'more than 50% of the TLC's active yellow taxi fleet is wheelchair accessible' as of June 2025, about 5,100 vehicles. The TLC's Accessible Dispatch program completed over 66,000 trips in 2024, about 5,500 a month.

taxis.unit: minimum share of each taxicab company's fleet that must be wheelchair accessible
taxis.note: LADOT Taxicab Rules and Regulations, rule 522: 'Wheelchair Accessible Vehicles shall constitute at least two percent (2%) of the taxicabs' for which a company provides branding and administration. This is a regulatory floor, not a count of the actual fleet.

taxis.unit: estimated wheelchair-accessible taxicabs active mainly on on-demand service
taxis.note: City of Toronto 2024 vehicle-for-hire review: after inactive WAV owners and TTC-contracted WAVs are removed, only about 10 accessible taxicabs are active on demand. 97% of active WAV taxicabs are contracted to Wheel-Trans, and 384 accessible taxicabs are inactive ('on the shelf'). Taxicab owner licences numbered 4,808 at 1 December 2024. In 2023, 46% of WAV taxi trips had waits under 10 minutes, against 82% for non-accessible trips. A Toronto Taxicab Licence holder must register an accessible vehicle within 90 days.

taxis.unit: wheelchair-accessible taxis approved in Metro Vancouver
taxis.note: Passenger Transportation Board, 'Update 2017' (data as of May 2017), so the figure is old. A search summary of a newer source gave 473 of 2,635 (18%) for Metro Vancouver, but it was not confirmed. Taxi companies must keep part of their fleet accessible as a licence condition.

taxis.unit: share of licensed taxis (black cabs) wheelchair accessible
taxis.note: TfL Taxi and Private Hire Action Plan 2025: 'taxis must be wheelchair accessible' and 'All taxis are wheelchair accessible'. Required by the Conditions of Fitness. Private hire vehicles (minicabs) are not required to be accessible.

taxis.unit: wheelchair-accessible SPSVs at end-2025 (Ireland); share of taxi and hackney fleet
taxis.note: NTA SPSV Bulletin 2025: 'At the end of 2025, WAVs comprised 23% of the total SPSV fleet and 26% of the taxi and hackney fleet.' The 4,781 WAVs are national, not Dublin-only. 519 WAV grants were paid in 2025 and 430 WAV licences were added without grant support.
No official figure for wheelchair-accessible taxis was found. Only private wheelchair-taxi firms appeared in searches.

housing.unit: share of housing units wheelchair accessible (AHS 'Level 3')
housing.note: HUD, 'Accessibility of America's Housing Stock: Analysis of the 2011 AHS' (published 2015), Table 7: 0.15% wheelchair accessible; 3.76% 'livable' for moderate mobility difficulty (Level 2); 33.34% 'potentially modifiable' (Level 1: step-free entry plus bathroom and bedroom on the entry level, or an elevator). Elevator in the home: under 3% of units.

housing.unit: share of housing units wheelchair accessible, Los Angeles MSA
housing.note: Same report, Table 11A (2011 AHS): Level 1 36.79%, Level 2 2.85%, Level 3 0.07%. No New York or New Haven table was found in the report.

housing.unit: share of homes whose entrance needs no steps up or down
housing.note: HUD, 'Accessibility in Housing: Findings from the 2019 AHS'. Also: 5% of homes have a ramp, 1% a chairlift, stairlift or platform lift (6% either); 44% have a full bathroom and a bedroom on the entry level; 19% of households include someone with a mobility-related accessibility need.

housing.unit: share of homes with all four 'visitable' features
housing.note: English Housing Survey 2018-19 fact sheet, England-wide, not London-only. The four features are level access, a flush threshold, wide enough doorways and circulation space, and a WC at entrance level. Individual features in 2018: WC at entrance level 66%, wide doorways 32%, flush threshold 27%, level access 19%. The chart shows all four rising from 5% in 2009 to 9% in 2018; reading 9% as the 2018 all-four value matches Habinteg's citation. 2.3 million homes had at least one disability adaptation. No newer EHS figure was found.
No published share of wheelchair-accessible dwellings was found. See worthChecking for the 2021 Census share of apartments in buildings of 5 or more storeys, which is a proxy for elevator buildings.

parking.permit: NYC Parking Permit for People with Disabilities (PPPD)
parking.note: Effect confirmed: park 'At any metered parking space, Passenger or Commercial, without charge' and in No Parking zones, with exceptions such as hydrants, bus stops and loading zones. Valid only in NYC; out-of-state permits are not honoured for on-street parking. Neither the DOT page nor 311 states a fee, so it is null.
No fee for a permanent placard; temporary placards carry a fee ($6 per search results, not confirmed). Effect: metered spaces at no charge, and green (time-limited) curbs without time limits.

Temporary placard $5. Under state law, CGS 14-253a (Connecticut OLR report https://www.cga.ct.gov/2010/rpt/2010-R-0293.htm, confirmed), placard holders may park 'for an unlimited period of time without penalty, regardless of the time indicated by a (1) parking meter, or (2) sign'. This waives the time limit, not the payment. A search summary says New Haven requires placard holders to pay at meters and sells vouchers; newhavenct.gov returned 403, so that is unconfirmed.

City of Toronto: an APP holder 'may park at on-street parking meters, parking machines or mobile only zones without depositing a payment', for at most 24 hours. Not valid in Green P lots or on private property, and vehicles over 3,000 kg must pay. That the APP is free from ServiceOntario comes from a search summary of ontario.ca.

Permanent permits last 3 years; temporary permits 1-12 months. Hardship assistance is available. Effect in Vancouver: a search summary says holders must still pay meters and lots; vancouver.ca returned 403, so this is unconfirmed.

Up to £10 in England (Scotland £20, Wales free); usually lasts up to 3 years. Effect (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/the-blue-badge-scheme-rights-and-responsibilities-in-england/the-blue-badge-scheme-rights-and-responsibilities-in-england): at meters and pay-and-display, holders 'may park for free and for as long as they need to'. The scheme does not fully apply in the City of Westminster, the City of London, Kensington and Chelsea, or part of Camden, which run their own concessions.

The €35 fee and 2-year validity come from a search summary; citizensinformation.ie and ddai.ie returned 403. Effect confirmed on Dublin City Council's page (https://www.dublincity.ie/travel-and-transport/parking-dublin-city/accessible-parking-dublin-city/disabled-persons-parking-permit): 'You can park in an ordinary parking space for free for unlimited time.' Issued by the Disabled Drivers Association or the Irish Wheelchair Association.

parking.permit: SEMOVI disability licence plates (placas para personas con discapacidad)
parking.note: Press report (ADN40, 5 August 2026), up from 447 pesos previously. Effect: ecoParq meter zones are exempt for CDMX disability plates (a SEMOVI post on X says the same), plus exemption from Hoy No Circula. semovi.cdmx.gob.mx was not reachable.

employment.unit: employment-population ratio, %, age 16+, September 2026, seasonally adjusted
employment.note: '...the employment-population ratio, at 59.2 percent, changed little in September.' Labor force participation 61.8%; unemployment 4.2%.
Series LNS12300060. 2026 monthly values: Jan 80.8, Feb 80.7, Mar 80.7, Apr 80.7, May 80.8, Jun 80.2, Jul 80.4, Aug 80.4, Sep 80.7.

employment.unit: employment rate, %, age 15+, August 2026, seasonally adjusted
employment.note: LFS, released 2026-09-04. Unemployment 6.4%. The September LFS is due after this read date.

employment.unit: employment rate, %, age 15+, Toronto CMA, August 2026, seasonally adjusted
employment rate, %, age 15+, Vancouver CMA, August 2026, seasonally adjusted

employment.note: ONS Labour market overview, 15 September 2026. No 25-54 or London figure was in the bulletin; London is in the separate regional release.
Down from 74.7% in Q2 2025. Men 78.0%, women 70.7%. The highest rate by age was 45-54 at 85.8%. 2,839,300 people in employment. No 25-54 or Dublin figure was in the release.

Derived: INEGI publishes participation of 59.3% and ocupada as 97.0% of the economically active population, and 0.593 x 0.970 = 0.575. 60.7 million employed; unemployment 3.0%. INEGI does not print an employment-to-population ratio.

employment.unit: employment-to-population ratio, %, age 15+, Ciudad de México, Q2 2026 (derived)
employment.note: Derived from INEGI ENOE Q2 2026 (bulletin 503/26, 25 August 2026): CDMX participation 62.9% and unemployment 4.2%, so 62.9 x 0.958 = 60.3. National Q2 2026: 60,040,094 employed of 104,305,022 aged 15+ = 57.6% (derived).

schedules.unit: share of wage and salary workers who usually worked on Saturday and Sunday
schedules.note: BLS 'Job Flexibilities and Work Schedules — 2024-25', released 24 September 2026: 'Sixty-eight percent of wage and salary workers usually worked Monday through Friday, and 8 percent of workers usually worked on Saturday and Sunday.'

schedules.unit: share of wage and salary workers usually on a non-daytime schedule
schedules.note: 2024-25: 85% on a regular daytime schedule; 5% evenings and 3% nights; the rest on rotating, split, irregular or other shifts. 57% had flexible start and end times. 34% worked at home at least occasionally, and 28% had days they worked only at home.

schedules.unit: share of employed people who worked on an average weekend day, 2025
schedules.note: ATUS 2025, released 25 June 2026: '81 percent of employed people worked on an average weekday, compared with 30 percent on an average weekend day.' Full-time workers worked 8.1 hours on the days they worked.

schedules.unit: average weekly hours, all employees, private nonfarm payrolls, September 2026
schedules.note: 'The average workweek for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls remained at 34.4 hours in September.'

schedules.unit: average usual weekly hours, permanent employees, August 2026
schedules.note: Not seasonally adjusted. Permanent full-time 39.1 and part-time 18.8; temporary employees 31.4 overall.

schedules.unit: share of workers with a regular evening shift or evening hours, April 2022
schedules.note: Quality of Employment in Canada. Regular night shift: 1.7% of workers aged 15-69, about 323,000 people (https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/n1/pub/14-28-0001/2023001/article/00008-eng.htm, confirmed). No Canadian weekend-work share was found.

schedules.unit: share of workforce who usually work in the evening or at night, 2022
schedules.note: ONS 'The night-time economy, UK: 2022': 27% (about 8.7 million) are night-time workers. 4% work only evenings or nights, 23% work evenings or nights as well as days, and 73% work only during the day.

schedules.unit: share of workers who work weekends
schedules.note: Search summary only (University of Sheffield paper using UK survey data): 31% work weekends, 37% work evenings and 16% work nights. No ONS weekend-work figure was confirmed.

schedules.unit: average actual weekly hours, full-time workers, May-July 2026, seasonally adjusted
schedules.note: Search summary only; the ONS bulletin text did not show it. ONS notes that an LFS operational issue in May 2026 noticeably affected its average-hours estimates.

schedules.unit: average hours worked per week per person employed, Q2 2026 (derived)
schedules.note: Derived: 89.0 million total weekly hours divided by 2,839,300 employed. 20.8% of the employed worked part-time.

schedules.unit: average hours worked per week, employed population, Q2 2026
schedules.note: 6.8% worked under 15 hours, 48.0% worked 35-48 hours and 23.2% worked over 48 hours. No ENOE evening or weekend share was found.

socializing.unit: minutes per day socializing and communicating, all days, 2025
socializing.note: ATUS 2025: 35 minutes, down from 41 in 2015. 30% did any on an average day, against 38% in 2015. Table 1 gives 0.58 hours. Table A-1: men 0.52 h, women 0.65 h; those who socialized averaged 1.92 h.

socializing.unit: minutes per day socializing and communicating, weekdays, 2025
socializing.note: Table 2 gives 0.44 hours (converted here: 0.44 x 60). 28.4% engaged on an average weekday.

socializing.unit: minutes per day socializing and communicating, weekends and holidays, 2025
socializing.note: Table 2 gives 0.92 hours (0.92 x 60). 35.2% engaged on an average weekend day or holiday. Check: (5 x 0.44 + 2 x 0.92)/7 = 0.577, which matches the all-days 0.58.

notFound: Metro-North New Haven Line: share of Connecticut stations that are accessible.
Vancouver: share of TransLink's conventional bus fleet that is accessible.
Mexico City: RTP, trolleybus and concession bus fleet accessibility shares; any government paratransit service; wheelchair-accessible taxi counts.
Dublin: a door-to-door paratransit service (none appears to exist); a Dublin-only WAV count (the NTA figure is national); a DART accessible-station count from Irish Rail.
New Haven: wheelchair-accessible taxi count or requirement.
Wheelchair-accessible or visitable housing shares for Canada, Ireland and Mexico. Newer English Housing Survey 'visitable' figures than 2018-19. New York-specific AHS accessibility figures.
NYC PPPD permit fee (no fee is stated on DOT or 311 pages).
Employment rates for ages 25-54 in the UK, Ireland and Mexico (published by other age bands only); London and Dublin regional employment rates.
Weekend-work shares from ONS, StatCan or INEGI; time use (socializing minutes) for Canada, the UK, Ireland and Mexico.
worthChecking: TfL step-free count: 94 in the March 2026 release, plus Northolt if it opened in summer 2026. A search summary also mentioned two step-free stations opening in September 2026. tfl.gov.uk blocked automated reads; a manual check of https://tfl.gov.uk/transport-accessibility/step-free-access would settle it.
TTC: 63 of 70 (Wikipedia, January 2026) plus Greenwood (February 2026, per TTC). Lawrence, College, Museum, Spadina, King and Islington were due in 2026-2027.

Mexico City Metro: 85 of 195 stations are marked accessible on the official map, against 57 working (Milenio, December 2024). metro.cdmx.gob.mx/tramites-y-servicios/accesibilidad-en-estaciones refused connections from here.
HandyDART fare: the publisher's page gives $3.50 adult cash from 1 July 2026, while a search summary said $3.35 cash and $2.70 stored value. Recheck the rider's guide PDF.
New Haven: whether placard holders must pay at city meters (search summary says yes, and that vouchers are sold), against the state law, which waives only the time limit.
Vancouver: whether SPARC permit holders pay at city meters (search summary says yes).
Vancouver accessible taxis: the 2017 PT Board figure (370 of 1,952) is old. A newer unconfirmed figure is 473 of 2,635 (18%).

Canada 2021 Census: 10.7% of occupied private dwellings are apartments in buildings of 5 or more storeys (30.7% in the Toronto large urban centre), from a search summary. This is a proxy for elevator buildings, not an accessibility measure.
UK full-time average actual weekly hours of 36.7 for May-July 2026 (search summary); confirm against ONS HOUR01 SA.
Access-A-Ride fare: $3.00 from 4 January 2026 per a search summary of an MTA fare document. The equal-to-full-fare rule itself is confirmed.
